question: To resolve peace following the riots that followed the Partition, the ‘Delhi Pact’ was signed between the Indian Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, and the Pakistan Prime Minister, __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Liaquat Ali Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Delhi Pact,' also known as the Nehru-Liaquat Pact, was signed on **8th April 1950** by Jawaharlal Nehru, the Prime Minister of India, and Liaquat Ali Khan, the Prime Minister of Pakistan.
 
• The pact aimed to address the concerns of minorities in both countries following the violence and displacement caused by the Partition of India in 1947.
 
• It was designed to ensure the safety and security of religious minorities in both nations and promised measures to protect their rights, properties, and cultural freedom.
 
• The agreement also aimed to curb the migration of people across borders and create an environment of peace and trust between the two newly created nations.
 
• Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, played a crucial role in the implementation of this pact and in shaping early Pakistan's domestic and foreign policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Muhammad Ali Jinnah**

 
 
• Jinnah was the founder of Pakistan and served as its first Governor-General until his death in 1948.
 
• He was the leader of the All-India Muslim League and played a pivotal role in the creation of Pakistan as a separate homeland for Muslims.
 
• While Jinnah was instrumental in the Partition of India, he passed away before the Nehru-Liaquat Pact was signed.
 
 
 
• **Malik Firoz Khan Noon**
 
 
• He served as the seventh Prime Minister of Pakistan from December 1957 to October 1958.
 
• He is also known for his efforts in incorporating Gwadar into Pakistan during his tenure as Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **Benazir Bhutto**
 
 
• Benazir Bhutto was the first woman to head the government of a Muslim-majority country, serving as Prime Minister of Pakistan in the late 1980s and 1990s.
